I know the timing is terrible, Xin Yi, but we need to figure out a plan for the pitch. The deadline is Thursday morning.
I've put the issue on the table. Now I'll wait to see how she and the others react.

Waiting for a response to my question.

I have to be at the wake. It's for the next two days.
I've stated my constraint. Now I need to see how they react and what they suggest.

This means she's completely unavailable to work on her section, which is only half done. This is a huge problem. I need to confirm the implications of this and figure out a way forward. The team can't easily take over her work. The best I can do right now is ask if she can at least hand over her work properly so we can even attempt to finish it. It's a delicate situation, but the project is at risk.
Okay, of course. We understand. Before you go, could you walk one of us through what's left to do on your section?
I've asked for a handover. This is the most practical step I can think of right now.

STRATEGY: ACCEPT. Suresh's suggestion is a practical way to handle the work. I need to be with my family, but I can't just leave the team with a problem. A handover is the right thing to do. It solves their problem and shows I'm responsible.
Okay. I can do that.
I've agreed to the handover. Now we'll need to sort out the details.

Waiting for Lakshmi or Meena to volunteer.

I can't. I'm still covering for Anil.
I've stated my inability to take on more work and am waiting for a response.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Lakshmi just said no, so now Suresh is looking at me. I absolutely cannot take this on. My own work is behind, and I've never done this type of analysis before. My section is behind too. And I don't know how to do that analysis.
Waiting for a response.

Lakshmi said no, and now Meena says she can't do it and doesn't have the skills. So there's nobody to take my work. My plan to hand it over and leave is stuck. I need to get to the wake. The only person who hasn't said no is Suresh. He's the one who suggested this plan. I'll wait to see what he says next.
Waiting for the team to resolve who will take over my work.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. So Lakshmi can't do it and Meena says she can't either. We're running out of options and time. The deadline isn't moving. I can't do all of Xin Yi's work plus my own. The only way forward is to split the work between the three of us. I'll have to take the hardest part, the analysis itself, but they have to pick up the other pieces. I need to lay out a clear plan right now.

Okay, we'll have to split it between the three of us then. After Xin Yi's handover, I'll take the main analysis. Meena, maybe you can handle the data and the charts? Lakshmi, can you work on integrating it all?
I've proposed a plan to divide the work. Now I'm waiting for their response.

I have clearly restated my position and am waiting for a response.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Lakshmi is refusing her part of the plan because she's already overloaded. I understand that, but what choice do we have? I've responded to Lakshmi's objection. I need to see if she'll accept this or if we're still at an impasse.

I've made the situation non-negotiable. Now I wait for them to respond to the new reality.

I'm going to put the responsibility back on her to propose a way forward.

I've proposed alternative solutions and am waiting for a response.

I've supported Lakshmi's suggestion for an extension. Waiting to see the response.

The time for being vague is over.

I've laid out the biggest constraint. Now they have to deal with it.
